note: Mexico informal: la mayo.

ex_es: El mezcal de Oaxaca es famoso.

ex_en: Mole poblano has chocolate in it.
note: Mexico: rich sauce of chilies, spices (and sometimes chocolate).

ex_en: I eat papaya with lime for breakfast.
I have lots of mosquito bites.

ex_es: Compré una playera en el mercado.
ex_en: I bought a T-shirt at the market.
note: Mexico: playera. Spain: camiseta.

ex_es: La regadera no tiene agua caliente.
ex_en: The shower has no hot water.
note: Mexico: regadera. Elsewhere: ducha.

ex_en: They sell tamales on the corner.
note: Singular tamal (not 'tamale'), plural tamales.

ex_es: Los domingos hay tianguis en mi colonia.
ex_en: There's a street market in my neighborhood on Sundays.
note: Mexican word (from Nahuatl). Invariable plural.

ex_es: Una tostada de ceviche, por favor.
note: Mexico: a flat crispy tortilla with toppings. Spain: toast.

ex_es: El zócalo está lleno de gente.
ex_en: The main square is full of people.
note: Mexico: el Zócalo = main square of a city (Mexico City's is huge).

ex_es: Un agua fresca de jamaica, por favor.
note: Feminine but el agua: el agua fresca. Flavors: jamaica, horchata, tamarindo.

ex_es: Un elote con mayonesa y chile, por favor.
ex_en: A corn on the cob with mayo and chili, please.
note: Mexico (Nahuatl). esquites = corn kernels in a cup.

ex_es: Una quesadilla de flor de calabaza.
Ponte bloqueador, el sol está fuerte.
ex_en: Put on sunscreen, the sun is strong.
note: Mexico: bloqueador (solar). Elsewhere: protector solar.

ex_es: Compra seis bolillos para las tortas.
ex_en: Buy six rolls for the sandwiches.
note: Mexico: crusty white bread roll.

ex_es: Las maletas van en la cajuela.
ex_en: The suitcases go in the trunk.
note: Mexico: cajuela. Spain: maletero.

ex_es: Me disfrazo de catrina para Día de Muertos.
ex_en: I dress up as a Catrina for the Day of the Dead.
note: Iconic Day of the Dead figure created by José Guadalupe Posada.

ex_es: Las flores de cempasúchil guían a los muertos.
note: Day of the Dead flower (Nahuatl). Also spelled cempazúchitl.

ex_es: Nadamos en un cenote en Yucatán.
ex_en: We swim in a cenote in Yucatán.
note: Yucatán: natural limestone sinkhole with fresh water.

ex_es: En la glorieta, tome la segunda salida.
ex_en: At the roundabout, take the second exit.
note: Mexico: glorieta. Spain: rotonda.

ex_es: Me compré unos huaraches en el mercado.
ex_en: I bought some huaraches at the market.
note: Mexico. Also a long oval masa dish.

ex_es: Un licuado de plátano, por favor.
note: Mexico: licuado = blended milk-and-fruit drink.

ex_es: Caminamos por el malecón al atardecer.
ex_en: We walk along the boardwalk at sunset.
note: Mexico: el Malecón (Puerto Vallarta, Veracruz, La Paz).
Mexico: nopales are eaten grilled or in salads.

ex_en: We take a minibus to Coyoacán.
note: CDMX: pesero / micro = shared minibus.
Mexico: popote. Elsewhere: pajita, sorbete.

ex_es: El pozole es típico en septiembre.
note: Mexican hominy soup; rojo, verde or blanco.

ex_es: Esa taquería abre toda la noche.
ex_en: That taco place is open all night.

ex_es: Voy a la tortillería por un kilo.
ex_en: I'm going to the tortilla shop for a kilo.
note: Mexico: shop that makes and sells fresh tortillas by weight.
Usually plural: totopos.
